title: Noetherian smooth Rees geometry for a closed section
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), let $d\geq0$, and let $g:V\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type of pure relative dimension $d$, with a closed section $s:S\hookrightarrow V$, $g s=1_S$.
For the ideal $\mathcal I$ of $s(S)$ set $\mathcal E=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$, $\pi:N_s=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)\to S$, with zero section $z$. Set $D_sV=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_V\mathcal O_V[t,\mathcal I/t]$, using the subalgebra of $\mathcal O_V[t,t^{-1}]$ generated by $t$ and the $b/t$, $b\in\mathcal I$. Its structural map is $q:D_sV\to\mathbf A^1_S$ and its section $\sigma$ is the augmentation $t\mapsto t$, $\mathcal I/t\mapsto0$, with coefficients restricted by $s$.
The conormal is locally free of rank $d$. The scheme $D_sV$ is Noetherian, $q$ is smooth separated of finite type and pure relative dimension $d$, and $\sigma$ is closed. Both $q$ and $\pi$ are compactifiable. There are canonical identifications of pairs
$$(q,\sigma)|_{t=1}\cong(g,s),\qquad(q,\sigma)|_{t=0}\cong(\pi,z),\qquad(D_sV,\sigma)|_{t\ne0}\cong(V,s)\times_S\mathbf G_{m,S}.$$
The zero-fibre identification is induced by $[b]_m\mapsto[b t^{-m}]$ from the associated graded algebra to $\mathcal O_V[t,\mathcal I/t]/(t)$ and the canonical symmetric-to-graded map. For every centred affine etale chart $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\to B$ with $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)B$, the corresponding open in $D_sV$ has algebra
$$B[t,I/t]\cong B\otimes_P R[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d],\qquad x_j\mapsto t u_j.$$
These opens, together with the punctured deformation, cover $D_sV$. The bundle and deformation, all open restrictions to Noetherian chart sources, and all separated finite-type chart maps and structural composites are between Noetherian schemes and are compactifiable. Here compactifiable means admitting an open immersion into a scheme proper over the target.
The scheme, morphism, algebra and coefficient notation and the specified comparison maps are those of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], [def-asd-compactifiable], [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Local construction, Rees charts, two fibres, Noetherian and compactifiable geometry; old item Steps 3–4.

proof.text: Apply the existing centred-coordinate theorem to the given smooth separated finite-type map and closed section. Its hypotheses are exactly those here, including pure dimension $d$ and Noetherian $S$. It gives affine neighbourhoods of the section with $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\to B$ etale, $I=(x)B$, and $B/I=R$. It also gives local freeness of $\mathcal E$ of rank $d$ and the canonical symmetric-to-associated-graded isomorphism, with the prescribed monomial formula. Use these actual ideal-class frames for the bundle throughout.

source.place: Local construction: centred coordinates and the Cartesian square of centres; Stacks 054L and 067U.

proof.text: For an ambient affine $\operatorname{Spec}B$ write $E=B[t,I/t]$. Restriction to a principal open $D(f)$ gives $E_f=B_f[t,I_f/t]$: its generators are $t$ and $(b/f^r)/t=(b/t)/f^r$, and both sides inject into $B_f[t,t^{-1}]$ (a Laurent polynomial localizes coefficientwise). Thus these are the associated module sheaves on the affine pieces, hence glue as a quasi-coherent algebra by the affine-local definition. The relative-spectrum theorem realizes their spectra as the corresponding opens of $D_sV$. The maps $B[t]\to E$ similarly give the associated algebra sheaves on $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$, agreeing on overlaps; their relative spectra give the same affine pieces. Thus $D_sV\to\mathbf A^1_V$ is affine: over an ambient affine it is $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$, and over a principal open in the latter its source is the spectrum of the same localization of $E$. Its composite with $\mathbf A^1_V\to\mathbf A^1_S$ is $q$.

source.place: Tag 01LX (lemma-spec-properties), affine construction and localization of the displayed extended Rees algebra.

proof.text: Coefficient reduction $B\to B/I$ on Laurent polynomials restricts to a surjection $E\to(B/I)[t]$: a negative coefficient in degree $-m$ belongs to $I^m$, so vanishes modulo $I$, while the constants and $t$ generate the target. This gives the stated augmentation section over the closed centre, and $q\sigma=1$ because $t$ is fixed and $gs=1$. After inverting $t$, one has $E[1/t]=B[t,t^{-1}]$, by the two inclusions of generators. Modulo $t-1$, every $b/t$ equals $b$, so evaluation gives $E/(t-1)\cong B$, inverse to the constants. All these formulas commute with localization in $B$. They therefore identify the punctured pair with $(V,s)\times_S\mathbf G_{m,S}$ and the pair at $1$ with $(g,s)$.

source.place: Local construction, the coordinates $u_i=x_i/t$; direct affine computation of the augmentation and punctured and one fibres.

proof.text: For each ambient affine apply the general extended-Rees associated-graded chart: $\operatorname{gr}_I B\xrightarrow{\sim}E/(t)$ sends $[b]_m$ to $[bt^{-m}]$. Combine it with the symmetric-to-graded isomorphism from Step 1 and the conormal algebra's normalized affine descriptions. The formulas commute with restrictions: localizing sends both representatives to $b/f^r$ in the same degree, and multiplication is multiplication of representatives. Relative-Spec base change identifies quotienting by $t$ with the scheme fibre. These affine comparisons consequently glue to the canonical $t=0$ identification with $N_s$. The augmentation sends positive homogeneous degrees to zero and degree zero to itself, so the section becomes precisely $z$ and the structural map becomes $\pi$.

For every centred affine etale chart in the statement, apply the existing etale-Rees-chart lemma with its $A=R$, $C=P$ and $R=B$. It gives $B[t,I/t]\cong B\otimes_P R[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$ with $x_j\mapsto tu_j$, and says the induced map to $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,u]$ is etale and its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ smooth of dimension $d$. This applies to every such chart, not just the chosen cover from Step 1.

source.place: Local construction: deformation of the zero section is affine space, with $x_j=tu_j$.

proof.text: The chosen neighbourhoods from Step 1 cover $s(S)$. Outside that closed centre the ideal sheaf is the unit ideal. On any affine inside this complement, $1/t$ is then a generator of $B[t,I/t]$, hence $t$ is invertible there. Thus every point outside the punctured deformation lies over the centre and is in one of the centred deformation opens. These opens and the punctured deformation cover all of $D_sV$.

source.place: Local construction: neighbourhoods of the section, completed by the punctured deformation.

proof.text: On the centred opens smoothness and pure dimension $d$ were proved in Step 5. On the punctured open the projection is the base change of $g$ by $\mathbf G_{m,S}\to S$, so it is smooth of dimension $d$ by smooth relative-dimension permanence. Smoothness is local on these affine neighbourhoods, as in the affine-local smoothness definition, and fibre dimension at a point is unchanged on an open neighbourhood. The cover of Step 6 therefore proves that $q$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$.

source.place: Local construction and punctured trivialization; Stacks 01VB and 02NK for the punctured projection.

proof.text: The base change $\mathbf A^1_V\to\mathbf A^1_S$ of $g$ is separated. The affine map $D_sV\to\mathbf A^1_V$ from Step 2 is separated by affine permanence, so their composite $q$ is separated by separated-composition permanence. Step 3 constructed $\sigma$ as a section of this separated map. The section-of-separated theorem makes $\sigma$ a closed immersion.

The affine-space projection $\mathbf A^1_S\to S$ is affine, hence quasi-compact, and locally finite type since over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ its algebra is generated by $t$. It is therefore finite type. Hence $V$ and $\mathbf A^1_S$ are Noetherian by finite-type-over-Noetherian, and $\mathbf A^1_S$ is quasi-separated. The relative-spectrum map $D_sV\to V$ is affine, hence quasi-compact; since $V$ is quasi-compact, its source $D_sV$ is quasi-compact by qcqs permanence (2). Now qcqs permanence (1) applied to $q$ makes $q$ quasi-compact. Step 7 makes it locally of finite presentation, so locally finite type: a finite polynomial presentation is in particular a finite generating set. Consequently $q$ is finite type, and finite-type-over-Noetherian applied over $\mathbf A^1_S$ proves $D_sV$ Noetherian.

Use the vector-bundle construction on the locally free $\mathcal E$ of Step 1. It supplies affine $\pi$ and trivializations $N_s|_U\cong\mathbf A^d_U$ with $z$ the zero section. The affine-space projections are smooth of dimension $d$; the same affine-local criterion as in Step 7 proves this for $\pi$. The polynomial coordinate rings show that $\pi$ is locally finite type, and affineness makes it quasi-compact and separated. Thus $\pi$ is separated finite type. Finite-type-over-Noetherian makes $N_s$ Noetherian. These facts include $d=0$, when the bundle is $S$.

source.place: Tag 01LX (lemma-spec-properties), vector-bundle local polynomial charts; Morphisms 01S7 and 01T6.

proof.text: Every open subscheme of the Noetherian schemes just obtained is Noetherian, so this includes all the indicated chart sources and their open restrictions. An inclusion of any such open into its ambient Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact by qcqs permanence (1) and etale by open-immersion etaleness, hence locally finite type and therefore finite type; it is separated directly from its diagonal, an isomorphism. All separated finite-type chart maps in the statement therefore have Noetherian ends. Their structural composites remain separated by composition permanence and locally finite type by the same permanence lemma (e); they are quasi-compact by qcqs permanence (1) because their sources are Noetherian and their targets quasi-separated. They are consequently finite type.

A Noetherian target is quasi-compact by definition and quasi-separated by the locally-Noetherian theorem. Apply Nagata compactification to each separated finite-type map proved above: $q$, $\pi$, the chart restrictions and chart maps, and their structural composites. Its statement gives an open immersion into a scheme proper over the target, which is exactly compactifiability as used here. Every application has a Noetherian, hence qcqs, target; no finite dimension or field hypothesis is imposed or used.

source.place: Nagata compactification theorem, the consequence for every separated finite-type morphism to a qcqs scheme.
